adds.title: Supreme Federal Court 2019 criminalization decision
adds.summary: On 23 May 2019 six of eleven Supreme Federal Tribunal justices voted to frame homophobia and transphobia as crimes under Brazil's 1989 racism law punishable by up to five years' imprisonment until Congress enacts specific sexual-orientation and gender-identity discrimination legislation, with the measure to take effect after the remaining votes on 5 June 2019.

adds.title: Rio Branco Bill No. 14/2024, Federal Public Prosecutor's Office criticism and mayoral veto
adds.summary: Rio Branco Bill No. 14/2024 proposed prohibiting minors from participating in the LGBT+ Parade, and the municipal government vetoed the bill following controversy including criticism from the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office.

adds.title: Brazilian Supreme Federal Court - March 2018 gender identity ruling
adds.summary: In March 2018 Brazil's Supreme Federal Court established that trans people can amend first name and gender on civil records by self-declaration without surgery, hormonal treatment or judicial authorization, securing nationwide legal gender recognition applicable in Alagoas.

adds.title: Court decision for Fênix da Silva Leite - October 15, 2021
adds.summary: On October 15, 2021, the Alagoas judiciary legally recognized Fênix da Silva Leite as a non-binary person, the first judicial recognition of non-binary identity in the state.

adds.title: Supreme Federal Court - 2019 gender identity discrimination prohibition
adds.summary: On 24 May 2019 six of eleven justices of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court voted to criminalize transphobia nationwide including Alagoas by treating it as equivalent to racism punishable under Brazil's racism law until Congress passes specific LGBT-protection legislation, with remaining votes scheduled for 5 June 2019.
